title: Micropatterning and Assembly of 3D Microvessels
protocol: Create a network pattern using CAD software.
Generate a mask of the network pattern.
Clean an 8" silicon wafer with oxygen plasma treatment for 5 min at 100 W.
Pour negative photoresist onto the wafer to form a dollop with a diameter of 2.5 cm.
Spin the wafer at 500 rpm with a ramp of 100 rpm/sec and maintain for 10 sec.
Ramp up to 1,600 rpm with a ramp of 300 rpm/sec and maintain for 30 sec.
Soft-bake the wafer at 65 °C for 7 min.
Ramp up to 95 °C with a rate of 360 °C/hr and maintain for 45 min.
Slowly cool down to room temperature on the hot plate.
Expose the coated wafer to 365 nm UV light under a chrome photomask, using an exposure triple that of the manufacturer's recommendation (350 mJ/cm²).
Hard-bake the exposed wafer at 65 °C for 5 min.
Ramp up to 95 °C with a rate of 360 °C/hr and maintain for 25 min.
Slowly cool down to room temperature on the hot plate.
Immerse the wafer in SU-8 developer for 10 - 15 min.
Clean the wafer with isopropyl alcohol.
Dry the wafer under a compressed nitrogen flow.
Inspect the pattern under a light microscope to ensure the SU-8 resist is well bonded to the wafer (look for unwanted peeling and bubbles).
Measure the thickness of the pattern features using a profilometer according to manufacturer's instructions.
Avoid regions essential for network function during measurement acquisition.
Alternatively, use a non-contact method (i.e., optical profilometer) to measure the thickness.
Place the wafer in a desiccator with 100 µl of trichloro(3,3,3-trifluoropropyl)silane for 2 hr to silanize the surface.
Transfer silanized wafer into a 120 x 120 mm square Petri dish.
Pour mixed and de-gassed PDMS elastomer and curing agent (10:1 w/w ratio) over the wafer to achieve 4 - 6 mm thickness.
Pour additional PDMS into a separate 120 x 120 mm square Petri dish to generate flat molds without patterns.
Cure at 65 °C for 2 hr.
Remove from oven and allow the PDMS to cool to room temperature.
Using a scalpel carefully cut a square around the SU-8.
Slowly peel off the PDMS mold from the wafer.
Trim edges to 30 mm x 30 mm.
For flat molds, cut cured PDMS without an imprinted pattern into square pieces about 40 mm x 40 mm.
Design the top housing piece to include a 20 mm x 20 mm well with a depth of 1 mm.
Place two collagen injection ports on the top of the device at the corners of the square well, each with a diameter of 4 mm.
Include two inlet and outlet reservoirs with diameters of 6 mm.
Drill four screw holes with a diameter of 3 mm at the four corners of the device for assembly purposes.
Design the bottom housing piece to include a central square hole with dimensions 15 mm x 15 mm.
Add a surrounding shelf around the central hole measuring 25 mm x 25 mm and 0.25 mm in depth.
Drill four screw holes with a 4-40 thread diameter on the bottom housing piece for alignment during assembly.
Wash two sets of tweezers, a stainless steel spatula, a small flat screwdriver, screws, and dowel pins.
Autoclave micropatterned PDMS molds, PDMS flat squares, glass coverslips (22 x 22 mm), and cotton pieces.
Sterilize PMMA housing pieces in bleach for at least one hour.
Rinse the sterilized PMMA pieces twice with autoclaved water.
Air dry the sterilized PMMA pieces in sterile tissue culture dishes.
Treat inner wells of sterilized dry PMMA pieces with plasma for approximately 1 min.
Add 1% Polyethyleneimine (PEI) onto the inner wells of the PMMA pieces for 10 min.
Rinse treated wells with sterile H2O and allow to dry in the tissue culture hood.
Apply 0.1% glutaraldehyde (GA) onto PEI-treated surfaces of the PMMA pieces for 30 min.
Rinse GA-treated surfaces twice with sterile water and allow to dry.
Fabricate vessels using collagen solutions ranging from 0.6% to 1%.
Determine the final volume (Vfinal) of gel required for vessel fabrication, typically 1 ml per device.
Calculate the volume (Vstock collagen) of stock collagen needed based on Vfinal and desired concentration (Cfinal).
Mix type I collagen stock solution with sodium hydroxide (NaOH), 10x Media Supplement (M199), and cell culture media to make 0.75% collagen for vessel fabrication.
Keep all solutions on ice during the mixing process.
Use a 1 ml syringe to transfer the appropriate volume of stock collagen to a new conical tube.
Determine volumes of neutralizing NaOH (VNaOH), M199 10x media supplement (V10X), and cell culture media (V1X) required separately in a conical tube.
Mix V10X, VNaOH, and V1X thoroughly before adding to the collagen solution.
Gently mix the collagen with the mixture of neutralizing reagents until a homogeneous gel is obtained.
Avoid introducing bubbles by stirring slowly and gently.
Place the micropatterned PDMS mold in a 100 mm x 20 mm dish.
Plasma clean the PDMS mold for 1 min.
Align the top PMMA piece on top of the PDMS mold so that the square reservoirs on the mold are directly under the inlet and outlet reservoirs.
Place the stainless steel dowel pins into the inlet and outlet reservoir holes on the top PMMA piece to maintain clear access from the reservoirs to the pattern.
Use a 1 ml syringe to extract ~ 0.5 - 0.6 ml collagen.
Ensure that no bubbles remain in the syringe.
Press down lightly with tweezers on the top housing to ensure flush contact between the top piece and the PDMS mold.
Inject collagen slowly through an injection port on the top PMMA piece.
Check that collagen fills in the 20 mm x 20 mm domain above the pattern and does not leak out.
Close the dish without jostling the dowel pins.
Allow to gel in a 37 °C incubator for 30 min.
Place a 22 x 22 mm glass coverslip in the center of the bottom piece.
Use a 1 ml syringe to dispense ~ 0.25 ml collagen evenly onto the glass slide.
Gently lower the PDMS flat square over the collagen, ensuring the PDMS is flat against the PMMA and there are no trapped bubbles.
Allow to gel at 37 °C for 30 min.
Add enough PBS around the flat PDMS piece on the bottom piece to surround the PDMS (about 1 ml).
Use tweezers to remove any excess collagen around the edges.
Slowly peel off the PDMS piece.
Add more PBS on top of the collagen to maintain hydration.
Pick up the top PMMA piece and flip it over so that the PDMS mold is on top.
Add a few drops of PBS to the interface.
Quickly and firmly remove the PDMS mold from the top PMMA piece.
Gently remove stainless steel dowel pins from the other side of PMMA housing using another pair of tweezers.
Add several more drops of PBS onto the micropatterned collagen.
Flip the PMMA top piece over so that the collagen faces down.
Place 4 screws into the corner holes of the PMMA top piece.
Gently lay the top piece on top of the bottom piece, aligning the screws with the corner holes on the bottom piece.
Do not allow the two pieces to slide against each other.
Use a screwdriver to tighten the screws using a gentle touch.
Aspirate the PBS surrounding the PMMA surfaces.
Place a small piece of cotton under one edge of the device.
Using a pipette, remove any PBS from the reservoirs.
Replace with cell culture media.
Allow the device to gel together in a 37°C incubator for at least 1 hr.
Culture human umbilical vein endothelial cells in endothelial growth media at 37 °C (CO2, O2) to confluency.
Trypsinize the cells by washing the culture flask with 6 ml of PBS and then adding 2 ml of 0.05% trypsin at 37 °C to dissociate the cells.
Stop the trypsin reaction by adding 4 ml of endothelial growth media containing fetal bovine serum (FBS).
Wash the flask several times with media to ensure cell detachment and collect in a conical tube.
Count the cells using a hemocytometer and resuspend them at a density of 10 million cells per ml.
Remove all cell culture media from the inlet and outlet reservoirs.
Add 10 µl of cell suspension into the center of the inlet reservoir.
Add 200 μl media equally to both reservoirs and let cells attach and spread within the network for at least 1 hr.
Culture the device with gravity driven flow through the network by adding 200 μl of cell culture media to the inlet reservoir and 50 μl to the outlet reservoir.
Replace media every 12 hr to maintain endothelial viability.
Dissolve 3.5% Dextran (70 kDa) in endothelial growth media for optimal vessel culture.
Fill 10 ml syringes with endothelial growth media containing 3.5% Dextran using sterile technique.
Prepare a sterile culture dish for flow by melting holes in the side wall of a Petri dish using a soldering iron.
Attach 12" silicon tubing (1/32" ID) to a Luer lock coupling (Female, 1/16" ID).
Attach a 1/16" straight tube-to-tube connector with a 1" segment of tubing on the other end.
Insert a 1/4" 20G blunt needle (detached from the needle hub) to the free end of the 1" segment.
Prepare a 3" segment of tubing attached to a tube-to-tube 90° elbow connector joint.
Autoclave all segments prior to use.
Thread autoclaved inlet and outlet tubing through holes in the prepared dish.
Attach 3" segments to inner 20 G needles.
Attach the Luer lock coupling to the media-filled syringe.
Perfuse media through the tubing using the syringe pump set at a high flow rate.
Ensure that there are no bubbles in the tubing or connectors, as these will impede flow to the vessel.
Insert the connector joint into the housing inlet.
Set the syringe pump to the desired flow rate and begin perfusion.
Collect perfusate with prepared outlet tubing inserted into a sterile 5 ml polystyrene round bottom tube containing 500 µl of media.
Add media to the collecting tube to prevent bubble formation that can block flow.
Refill the syringe after 24 to 36 hours by removing the connector from the housing inlet, replacing the syringe, and allowing media to perfuse at a high flow rate for several minutes.
Reset the pump to the desired flow rate for culture after refilling.
Insert the connector into the housing inlet and return to the incubator.
Place the vessel housing on a confocal microscope and focus at the vessel plane.
Add 5 μM 40 kDa FITC-Dextran to the inlet.
Image at 4X magnification with an exposure time of 25 msec, capturing one frame per second for 10 minutes.
Analyze the image series using analysis code to estimate the permeability of Dextran across the vessel wall into collagen (μm/sec).
Immunostain vessels by perfusing with 3.7% formaldehyde through the inlet for 20 min.
Wash fixed vessels by perfusing PBS three times (20 min per wash).
Block nonspecific antibody binding by perfusing 2% bovine serum albumin and 0.5% Triton X-100 for 1 hr.
Perfuse primary antibody solutions overnight at 4 °C.
Wash with PBS after overnight perfusion of primary antibodies three times.
Perfuse secondary antibody solutions for 1 - 2 hr.
Wash again with PBS following the application of secondary antibodies.
Acquire immunofluorescence images of microvessels in situ using a confocal microscope with a z-step of 1 µm.
Image microvessels at magnifications of 4X, 10X, or 20X for structural and cellular details.
Analyze image stacks using ImageJ with Z projections (Image/Stacks/Z-project), cross sections (Image/Stacks/Orthogonal view), and 3D reconstructions (Image/Stacks/3D Project).
Fix vessels in situ by perfusing half-strength Karnovsky's solution (2% paraformaldehyde/2.5% glutaraldehyde in 0.2 M cacodylate buffer) overnight for electron microscopy analysis.
Disassemble the vessel carefully after fixation and separate the two pieces.
Trim edges of the separated vessel pieces and fully immerse them in fixative solution for several days.
Immerse the thick top portion of the vessel in 25% glutaraldehyde for 20 min.
Rinse the vessel three times with PBS (2 min each).
Dehydrate the vessel in a serial ethanol wash starting at 50%, followed by 70%, and then 85% (each for 2 min).
Proceed with two washes of 100% ethanol, each lasting 5 min.
Further dehydrate the sample following the manufacturer's critical point drying protocol.
Sputter coat the vessel with gold-palladium (7 nm).
Analyze the vessel under a scanning electron microscope at an accelerating voltage of 5 kV and spot size 3.
